paras: While the size of Arctic sea ice has dropped by about 40 percent over 40 years, until recently, the size of the sea ice around Antarctica was slowly increasing. Then, after 2015, Antarctic ice extent (范围) fell from a record high to several record lows, losing an area as large as Greenland.

Some research has suggested that higher air temperatures may be the cause. However, two new studies show that ocean warming played a bigger role in this dramatic change. As part of global ocean circulation (全球海洋环流), warm saltwater moves southward from the tropics and circles Antarctica 200 metres below the surface. But temperature and saltiness records of the past 20 years suggest that this warm deep saltwater has been rising towards the surface, where it can melt (融化) sea ice.

Antarctica is encircled by a belt of strong winds and storms. Climate change has pushed this storm belt southward, bringing more rain and snow into the sea ice area, according to a study by Earle Wilson and other researchers at Stanford University. The rain and snow create a layer (层) of fresh surface water that better protects the bottom of the sea ice from warm deep saltwater, allowing it to grow to its 2014 record high. But the same southward-moving storm belt also brings stronger winds. These winds blow surface water and ice forward. As this happens, warm deep saltwater rises up to fill the empty space.

Between 2014 and 2016, this wind-driven rising began to get the upper hand against the protective layer of increased rain and snow, and sea ice began to melt away. When the researchers input the recorded ocean data (数据) into a computer model, it projected that sea ice would grow and then become smaller, as it did in the real world.

The researchers plan to study and model other things, which also likely play roles throughout Antarctica. Examples include changes in sea ice movement and increases in ocean mixing resulting from more storms. By studying the ocean data, they hope to build a model to project changes in Antarctic sea ice in the years to come.
source: 真题/2026年北京市中考英语试题.docx

paras: The internet has provided us with unmatched ways to get information, but it is also sounding alarms. Some experts argue that the internet will produce forgetfulness in the minds of those learning to use it, because they won’t practise their memory.

Is the internet really doing harm to our memories—or will our doubtful experts be proven wrong? After all, the brain’s attention system (系统) and preferences for novel experiences were already there long before the digital age, and our ability to remember is nearly inexhaustible (无穷尽的). According to Michael Merzenich, a brain researcher, every brain is a work in progress; it keeps changing throughout our lives, depending on how we use it.

But our brains don’t work well when we’re not focused. When we repeatedly check text messages and social media during work, we are weakening our ability to form both short- and long-term memories, experts say. The flood of information influences our ability to remember, too. Though our brains are designed to look for new data, too much of it may be causing this natural drive to go wild. The compulsion to continuously take in information means we often check social media when we should be doing “memory housekeeping” by giving our brains some rest. Another problem: the effortless way of receiving information online. Trying to actively recall (回忆) data is a good workout for the brain, but today we are using online search tools instead.

However, the internet may be changing only what we remember, not our ability to do so, suggests Columbia University psychologist (心理学家) Betsy Sparrow. In fact, the internet is becoming an outside hard drive for our memories. Some worry that this is having a negative effect on society, but Sparrow suggests this will change our way of learning from a focus on remembering facts to one on understanding ideas.

As is shown in a 2008 study, using the internet exercised the brain more than reading among older adults with strong computer skills. And two Harvard psychologists argue that not needing to remember facts might free our minds to focus on more meaningful tasks.

“There may be costs caused by our increased dependence on the internet, but generally the benefits are going to outweigh those costs,” says Benjamin Storm, a psychologist. “It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better? At this point, we don’t know.”
source: 真题/2026年北京市中考英语试题.docx

paras: A Chinese robot became the unexpected star in an international kite festival. At the beginning of the festival, the robot held the string (线) of a kite flying in the sky and made up-and-down movements. The show lasted for 20 minutes and drew crowds of visitors to take photos.

The robot in the international festival is a good example of human-like robots. In recent years, human-like running robots have greatly improved and surprised the world. This year, a robot from a Chinese company broke the men’s record for the half-marathon (半程马拉松). In another event, a robot, also from a Chinese company, came close to the men’s 100-meter world record.

Robots are not just for flying a kite or running in competitions. They are also helping on farms. Picking tomatoes is tiring work for humans. Now farming robots can help with it. The robots first get information about the tomatoes on their own. The information is about whether the tomatoes are ripe (成熟的) or not and whether there are any tomatoes hidden behind leaves. With the information, the robots can work out the most effective way to pick the fruit. When picking tomatoes, the robots must choose ripe tomatoes and leave unripe ones untouched.

There are many reasons for the rapid improvement of robots in recent years. The cost of building robots has fallen a lot. New computer chips allow machines to perform better. With the development of technology, robots are playing an increasingly important role in everyday life.
source: 真题/2026年河北省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Scientists have studied animals’ feelings for hundreds of years. However, the past research mainly focused on animals’ negative feelings, such as pain and fear. This can help reduce animals’ suffering, but it doesn’t tell what brings them happiness.

Now some scientists are working together to better understand animals’ joy. They are trying to measure (测量) joy in animals in a new study. The scientists define (下定义) joy as a strong positive feeling which is caused by an event, such as seeing a friend or a favorite food. They have created a set of ways to measure the feeling in different animals. The scientists want to make sure that the final result is not from just guessing animals’ minds, but from scientific research.

Some signs of joy are connected with actions. For example, some scientists have noticed that chimpanzees (黑猩猩) make laugh-like sounds while they are playing. Other scientists have noticed that dolphins (海豚) produce joyful sounds when happy things happen to them.

However, actions do not tell the whole story. Horses seem to be happily playing, but they may actually have the opposite feeling: they are downcast. So the scientists are also examining animals’ brain chemistry and studying their body temperature changes to help tell if the animals are truly happy.
Learning about joy in animals can improve the care of animals. And the new study about animals’ happiness can also help us better understand humans’ happiness.
source: 真题/2026年河北省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Packing for a family holiday often feels like a rush to remember necessary things like socks or medicine. However, for children, packing can be valuable because it helps them learn math in real life.

Counting is a basic math skill. Before they pack, children should first think about the activities in the holiday. Different activities require different things. Then they will count the days of the trip and how many things they will take. For example, if swimming is included, they may need to take swimming clothes. If the trip lasts seven days, they will consider how many clothes they need. In this process (过程), they practice counting.

Sometimes, the suitcase is not big enough. After they fail to pack everything in, children quickly learn the importance of space. They might try folding (折叠) their clothes in different ways to make them smaller. By trying again and again, children start to understand something like volume (容积).

More importantly, the questions from adults can guide children toward deep thinking. For example, when the mother sees her child put milk and clothes together, she may ask her child if it is OK to do so. The child has to consider whether it is proper to pack that way. If not, the child will think about what the proper way is. Deep thinking is what children need when they solve difficult math problems.
Learning math happens not only at a desk but also in other places. Therefore, when parents do housework, children should try to take part if possible.
source: 真题/2026年河北省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Ieoh Ming Pei was known as the master of modern architecture (建筑). He designed (设计) many famous buildings and landmarks around the world.

Pei was born in Guangzhou in 1917. He grew up in a family that valued education and traditional art. Suzhou was his ancestral hometown. Pei spent most of his childhood holidays there. During those holidays, he would visit the gardens whenever he had time. Seeing those rocks, stone bridges and waterfalls, he began to show interest in them. At the age of ten, Pei moved with his family to Shanghai. The city’s international architectural style had a strong influence on him. He decided to become an architect. In 1935, Pei went abroad to study. When he was 38, he started his company in New York. In 1983, he won the Pritzker Prize, the highest honor in architecture.

One of Pei’s most famous works is the glass pyramid in front of the Louvre Museum (卢浮宫) in Paris. It was completed in 1989. It showed his idea—let light design the buildings. Many people disliked it because it was so different from the traditional architecture at that time. But today, it is one of the most popular places in France. Suzhou Museum is another work of his. It opened in 2006 and became a must-see place later. Pei explained, “It should belong to Suzhou, but also to the world. It should be traditional, yet modern.” He created over 50 designs during his life.
Pei passed away in 2019 at the age of 102. His designs are regarded as gifts to the world.
source: 真题/2026年山西省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Last summer, we visited a bank in Kunming, but this bank holds life instead of money. It’s called the Germplasm Bank of Wild Species in Southwest China (中国西南野生生物种质资源库). Its seed (种子) bank, the largest one in Asia, keeps nearly 100,000 collections from over 11,000 kinds of wild plants.

We learned that many scientists made hard journeys to fill this bank. They climbed mountains, crossed highlands, and traveled through forests to collect valuable seeds. One scientist, Li Heng, led more than 20 trips to high mountains—even after the age of 61—and got badly hurt after falling from the back of a horse during her work. But nothing could stop her. She often said to her team, “Choose one thing, and give yourself to it.” Another scientist, Guo Yongjie, collected seeds from Mount Qomolangma at 6,212 meters above sea level. This is the highest place ever for collecting plant seeds. He spent over 200 days a year in the wild, just to add one more kind of plant seed to the bank.

“A seed is hope,” one scientist shared. These seeds are not just tiny plant parts; they carry genes (基因) that may help us grow better crops (庄稼), make new medicines, or bring back lost forests. But some kinds of plants are disappearing, and we may lose them forever. Therefore, collecting valuable seeds is a race against time. It is a job that needs patience, courage and love.

Saving seeds is everyone’s job. Such seed banks are not only found in China. By working with seed banks in Norway, the UK, and some other countries around the world, the scientists can turn these treasures into a shared hope for the far future.

As we left, we had a deeper respect for the scientists who have spent their lives on this quiet but great work. The seeds they save carry life, hope, and a better future for all living things on the earth.
source: 真题/2026年辽宁省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Ayi is a 22-year-old girl from Kashgar, Xinjiang. She became well-known in a new season of a TV programme, which tells people how young people build their careers after leaving school. The programme followed 12 students who studied Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM). As the youngest one, Ayi at first was unnoticed. By the end of the season, however, she surprised all with her great progress.

Ayi was not from a family of doctors. Her earliest interest in traditional medicine was awakened in her old town. In that place, people believed mutton soup cured illness faster than seeing doctors in hospital. When her grandmother died of illness, she realized good doctors were needed in that place. That was when she decided to become one to serve the people there.

In 2018, thanks to an education programme for Xinjiang middle school students, Ayi had a chance to study in a Shenzhen high school. Three years later, she was accepted by Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine.

However, the road to becoming a TCM doctor was never easy. For her, it was especially difficult to understand ancient Chinese medical books. “Terms (术语), like yin and yang, were a totally new way of thinking. So I was always half a step behind my classmates,” Ayi said. To catch up, she put in more time and developed a study method of her own. Along with her schoolwork, Ayi got practical experience by taking part in more than 13 volunteer activities.

Ayi’s greatest dream is to return to Xinjiang and use her TCM knowledge to serve local people. “Back in Kashgar, I know many people don’t look for medical care, so I believe it’s deeply meaningful to use TCM, which is simple and cheap and works well,” Ayi said.
source: 真题/2026年浙江省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Motorcycle helmets are important. They protect riders from getting hurt. In 2017, about 1,872 riders in the US were saved because of helmet use. Effective helmets do more than protect people in accidents. They also help keep wind and small flying pieces off riders’ faces.

Before the 1970s, motorcycle helmets were made of plastic, offering little protection. Today, they are made of carbon fibre (碳纤维), much lighter and stronger than before. Now, they are safer and more comfortable.

With the development of technology, modern helmets are smarter. Through Bluetooth-connected speakers, riders can make telephone calls as they travel along the road. Cameras are also found in modern helmets. They can record what is happening ahead like the cameras in cars, and they are easy to control by voice. The visors in certain helmets are able to change their colour. They become dark when the sun shines too brightly or when strong light from cars and trucks hits riders’ faces. In this way, riders can avoid strong light and see better.

These days, AI is changing people’s way of life. For motorcycle riders, AI can now be placed inside helmets to achieve greater safety. One such example is the iC-R smart helmet. This helmet can show the objects around the motorcycle. The riders don’t need to turn their heads or take their eyes off the road ahead to get a better sense of the road situation. The helmet can also receive all the important information, such as speed, direction and traffic accidents. When a rider decides where to go, the helmet shows different ways to get there on the inside of the visor. It can even warn the rider when necessary, like when a motorcycle gets too close to a car.
source: 真题/2026年浙江省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Ms. Beryl and Layla are great friends. It doesn’t matter that Beryl is 87, and Layla is four. The pair have many interests in common, and they spend a lot of time together. They make drawings, play games, and laugh at each other’s jokes. The two attend an intergenerational preschool called Mother Nurture. It brings society’s oldest and youngest members together in a community.

“At Mother Nurture the kids have someone who can tell great stories, but who also has the time and patience to really listen to them,” says director Penny Livingston. “Many of the children do not have grandparents in the same city, and their friendships with their elderly ‘classmates’ make it possible for them to get along with people at a different stage of life.”

For the elderly, the experience is also rewarding (有益的). The children bring the joy and excitement of youth into their lives, and the time spent with kids improves their health. The elderly report feeling less lonely. Their minds work better, and even their bodies seem to benefit from staying with the children because they move more.

Mother Nurture is just one of many such programmes that have appeared around the world. The programmes work and even the kids’ parents benefit. Many families do not have relatives nearby, and the chance for their children to spend time with a person like a grandmother or grandfather pleases parents.

“We kind of get stuck with people who are the same age as us,” says Maya, a caregiver who has worked at Mother Nurture for three years. “When I see how careful the children are around their older friends, I know they are developing empathy (共情) for people who are different,” she says. “And that is good news for the rest of us since we will all be old one day.”
source: 真题/2026年山东省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Every time you send an email, a message or a photo, or post something on the Internet, you save paper. However, you leave behind your digital carbon (碳) footprint.

You may think that the Internet has no effect on the physical world, but we store all the information on different websites, apps and social media on computer servers (服务器). They use lots of electricity. At the same time, they need to be cool, so we use more electricity to keep the temperature low. However, the production of electricity increases our carbon footprint and heats up our earth.

All information, pictures and music on the Internet travel in small packets of data (数据). So when we do an online search, the question we have put into the computer becomes data. The computer sends this data to the servers. They then process (处理) the question and send the answer back to our computers as data. The faster the search engine (引擎) works, the greater the use of electricity. We use the most electricity when we watch a video online. This is because a lot of data travels to and from the server.

Different kinds of technology need different amounts (量) of electricity to work. For example, mobile phones use electromagnetic waves. These waves need more energy to move through buildings, bad weather and even plants. So again, the use of electricity is greater. Cloud computing also uses a lot of energy because instead of saving your material on your computer, you store it on the server. So again, more data travels between the servers and the computers, using large amounts of energy.

One way to stop this waste is to always update your apps or software. For example, an old word processing tool needs four times more energy to work than a new one. Another way is to think before you see a film online: do you really need to see it for the tenth time?
source: 真题/2026年山东省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Do you like DIY? Have you ever tried magazine collaging (拼贴画)? There’s a reason why it is making a big comeback. It provides an easy way to relax and make something by hand while staying away from phones and computers.

This art form, including cutting pictures out of magazines and putting them onto a piece of paper, is full of fun. One of the best things about magazine collaging is how easy it is to start. Unlike other hobbies that require expensive materials or training, collaging lets you start with just a magazine, glue, and a pair of scissors.

Magazines are surely necessary materials for this hobby. If you don’t have magazines at home, find cheap or free ones at thrift stores (慈善商店). You can also use junk mail, stamps, and even packaging (包装). “These things can make your works more personalized,” says Ms. Drewett, a professional collage artist.

Once you have materials ready to go, it’s time to start cutting. What you need to do is to cut out all the pictures that interest you. Then consider having a theme to plan your pictures. Drewett says, “We explore all kinds of themes. Sometimes we focus on flowers for fun. Other times we talk about our daily life. We also get ideas from art history.”

When the pictures are well prepared, map them out on your paper. This is a fluid process and you might move things around several times. “I go back to my work again and again. It may take a few tries to get it right. Just follow your heart and enjoy yourself,” Drewett shares. Finally, when everything looks good, use the glue to stick them on the paper, and your work of art comes to life.

Magazine collaging is less about perfection and more about enjoying the act of making and self-expression. The beauty of this hobby is that anyone can create their own works with just a few materials and an active imagination.
source: 真题/2026年山东省济南市中考英语试题.docx

paras: On a hot summer afternoon, cities and towns are usually hotter than the nearby countryside areas. This is not just a feeling. Some cities can be as much as 7°C hotter. Scientists call this the “urban heat island” effect (城市热岛效应).

This effect is closely connected with the materials used in city buildings, which usually take in large amounts of heat from sunlight during the day. Instead of cooling quickly after sunset, these materials slowly give out the stored heat into the air. As a result, cities remain warm for a lot longer. In certain situations, high temperatures can even be deadly.

To cut urban heat, many cities have turned to trees, which work like natural air conditioners in two main ways. First, they provide shade (树荫), preventing streets and buildings from heating up too much. Second, trees cool the air through a process called transpiration—water inside the leaves enters the air, lowering temperatures nearby.

To understand how effective trees really are, researchers studied air temperature and tree cover data (数据) from nearly 9,000 cities, and the findings were surprising. Trees reduce the “urban heat island” effect by almost 50% all over the world. Since cities are usually 1–3°C hotter than nearby countryside areas, trees can lower temperatures by about 0.5–1.5°C in many places, which can have an influence on city heat during the long hot summer.

However, scientists warn that planting trees alone cannot completely solve the problem. Even with large planting projects, urban trees may cut down only a bit of heat by the middle of this century. Because of this, experts believe cities need more solutions. For example, reflective building materials can help. At the same time, ways of cutting greenhouse gases (气体) remain necessary.

Trees are powerful and valuable. They cool cities, improve air quality and make urban life more comfortable. But in a warming world, they work best as part of a larger plan rather than as the only answer.
source: 真题/2026年山东省济南市中考英语试题.docx

paras: Minqin, lying in the city of Wuwei in Gansu, is sandwiched between China’s third- and fourth-largest deserts. It is one of the country’s main sources (来源) of sandstorms. In 2007, then 26-year-old Ma Junhe started Minqin’s first environmental protection volunteer program named Save Minqin after reading in a newspaper that his hometown was at risk of being covered by sand within 17 years. The program started with just 60 volunteers. Last year, more than 6,000 volunteers planted suosuo trees there, most of whom were aged between 18 and 30, also called Gen Zers.

Zhang Liwen, an 18-year-old girl from Xi’an, spent five days planting suosuo trees in Minqin. “This idea came from my wish to complete a meaningful coming-of-age ceremony, but now I find value in contributing (贡献) to society,” Zhang said. The vlogs shared by Zhang are lively and attractive. She filmed a group of young volunteers, including herself, planting trees with stylish sports sunglasses, enjoying local noodles in their tent, and dancing in the desert after work.
Li Xiuniang, from Heilongjiang province, also posted her volunteer work online. “This task isn’t just for Minqin; it’s for all of China,” she said.

Lee Ting-Hsuan, a 20-year-old student from Taiwan, is one of thousands of volunteers who travel to Minqin every year. Around 20 young volunteers from Macao also joined the program. “Through tree planting, we get a deeper understanding of Northwest China and its culture,” one of them said.

Since 2007, over 80,000 volunteers have joined this program and they have planted over 1.52 million trees, making a green promise in the yellow sands. Ma Junhe said, “Gen Zers are more confident in achieving their dreams. They really enjoy meaningful public activities, and help a lot by sharing their stories online, attracting more people to take action.”
source: 真题/2026年山东省烟台市中考英语试题.docx

paras: Recently, researchers have discovered a new bacterium (细菌) that feeds on plastics. Scientists say the discovery could help reduce a flood of plastics that are ending up in the landfills (垃圾填埋场) and polluting oceans.

Plastic is one of the most difficult materials to break down or recycle. To solve the problem, a team from the Helmholtz Center for Environmental Research in Germany found the new soil bacterium. It was found in an area with a lot of plastic wastes. The team discovered the bacterium could feed on polyurethane (聚氨酯), which is widely used in making different plastic products.

It was reported that polyurethane made up 3.5 million tons of Europe’s plastics last year. One problem is that recycling polyurethane requires a lot of energy. So most polyurethane-based wastes are sent to landfills, where they can give off dangerous chemicals.

The team found that the bacterium could produce enzymes (酶) that could eat polyurethane. This would make it possible to break down plastic wastes. The results were recently reported in a science magazine.
Hermann Heipieper helped write the report. He said that the finding “marks an important step in being able to reuse hard-to-recycle products”.

The research is part of a European Union program that tries to find useful bacteria. The goal is to discover living things that can help turn plastics into materials that can be broken down biologically.

Some scientists advise against introducing the bacteria into the environment at present, which could be harmful. It is suggested that much more study should be carried out to learn more about the bacterium. “Such research is needed before we can take action such as putting the plastic-eating bacteria into the oceans,” a scientist said.
source: 真题/2026年山东省烟台市中考英语试题.docx

paras: Did you notice how nature sometimes repeats itself? Something that repeats is called a pattern. There are many patterns for you to study and learn.

Look around you. Patterns are everywhere. You may see bright and colorful patterns if you look at fish in the sea. In a bee’s honeycomb, the six-sided shape is repeated many times. Some leaves always have five points on them.

Listening carefully, you will find a noisy world. Dogs bark, the rain falls and the wind blows. Are these patterns? Of course! Sounds that repeat are patterns. A cricket (蟋蟀) uses its wings to make repeated chirping (啁啾叫) sounds. Do you know that a cricket’s chirp changes with the temperature? The hotter it is, the more chirps a cricket will make.

Try to find out how living things grow around you. Seeds (种子) grow into plants. A butterfly begins life as an egg. Each living thing has its own pattern as it grows. When a human baby is born, it is small. With time, the baby learns to lift its head and learns to roll over. Finally, the baby learns to stand up and walk. This kind of pattern is called a pattern of development.

If something happens over and over, it, too, forms a pattern. For example, you get up at 7:00 every morning. You get dressed and then eat breakfast at 7:30 a.m. If you repeat this many times, it becomes a pattern. Having a music class every Monday is a pattern. So is going to school five days a week and having Saturday and Sunday off.
It seems as if the world is full of patterns. Just think—without patterns, the world would be much harder to study!
source: 真题/2026年河南省中考英语试题.docx

paras: For most foreign teenagers, learning Chinese poems could be boring. But for a group of exchange students in China, it became an amazing trip. To help them learn more, Chinese students in a middle school started a club called “Poetry Gathering”.

In this club, students explored the classic poems in active and creative ways. Chinese students prepared “fun cards”. On the cards were famous poems and theme (主题) paintings. Cards about Li Bai’s moon, Du Fu’s mountains, and Wang Wei’s desert were popular. They helped the exchange students know how ancient poets used Chinese to “paint” pictures.

Besides, students used simple instruments like drums to experience the rhythm (节奏) of the poems. “When I play the drums to a Tang poem, I can hear the music hidden in the lines,” said Alice, an exchange student. “It makes the poem easy to sing out loud and interesting to share.” By putting poems, paintings and the rhythm together, students made the club a fun place where ancient poets met their teenage fans.

When Chinese students and exchange students studied together, they both benefited greatly. “To help them better understand our poems, I have to do some closer reading. Each character means a lot in poems. For example, 水 (shui) shows beauty, sweetness, and a smooth feeling,” said Li Ran. “When my new foreign friend said he could feel the imagery (意境) of the lines, I felt very proud of our culture,” Li added.

In fact, learning poems can be fun for everyone. These activities not only offer students a chance to learn more about Chinese poems, but also bring people of different languages and cultures together.
source: 真题/2026年湖北省中考英语试题.docx

paras: In ancient China, letters were sent by pigeons and packages (包裹) by horses. Common people could hardly afford it. In 1896, China opened its very first post office. That was the beginning of China’s own postal service. With a small stamp on the cover, people in big cities could send letters and packages. Bikes, ships and trains carried them across mountains and rivers in the country, even abroad.

After the founding of the People’s Republic of China in 1949, the postal service grew rapidly. Post offices were set up all around the country. Their services stretched to even the quietest, farthest villages. That made communication much easier for people in every corner of the country. College students could write to their parents in faraway hometowns. Friends and relatives could send packages on festivals to greet each other.

Since the 1990s, a new branch (分支) of postal service, the delivery (快递) industry, has also grown rapidly. Take the year 2025 for example. Every second, over 6,000 packages were on the move. Every day, more than 500 million packages were processed and put into trucks. In the whole year, over 180 billion were sent across the country. And the fastest delivery took only several hours!

Now, “speed” is no longer the only key word in this industry. Many delivery services have started to go green. Each year, more than 800 million boxes are reused or recycled. Besides, smart packing models are widely used. There’s no doubt that delivery services are smart in our life and friendly to our environment.

From pigeons and horses to delivery trucks, China’s postal history shows how this great old nation has developed and progressed. Looking forward, will China’s postal service fly to the moon and other planets in outer space?
source: 真题/2026年湖北省中考英语试题.docx

paras: The ocean covers most of our planet, yet we know very little about it. Our ocean is as mysterious as it is beautiful. In fact, we have better maps of Mars than we do of the ocean floor. Why? Exploring (探索) the ocean is a really hard job. There’s a lot of ocean—about 1.4 billion trillion litres (升). That’s 1,400,000,000,000,000,000,000!
But many scientists are taking on this challenge. One of their most important goals is to learn about coral reefs (珊瑚礁), which are home to lots of sea plants and animals.
Do you know that coral is an animal, not a plant? Tiny animals called polyps (珊瑚虫) build the hard part of the coral as a home to live in. They are called “architects” in the ocean.
However, many coral reefs around the world are in danger. That’s where a clever method called “coral gardening” comes in—giving reefs a second chance. Here’s how it works in four steps:

First, scientists collect small pieces of coral from coral reefs. Then they break them into even smaller ones—tiny pieces grow faster. After that, they place the pieces in lab-controlled or underwater nurseries (苗圃), where tiny pieces are taken good care of. Finally, once strong enough, they are planted onto rock or man-made reefs so that they can grow on their own.
A typical example is the L-shaped Reef. Since 1982, scientists have placed old subway cars into the sea. These strange “homes” have created a huge man-made reef. Now, polyps and fish are moving in!

To know more about the ocean, a volunteer, Paul Green, started the Big Bag Project in 2025. It calls on beach visitors to help collect information on plastics and water temperature through a bag which is connected with an app. Next time you go to the beach, take a bag, pick up some rubbish, and have a closer connection with the ocean.
source: 真题/2026年湖北省武汉市中考英语试题.docx

paras: AI is used to help solve problems in many fields now. Here’s how it helps save energy, protect animals, and reduce pollution.

In many office buildings, people sometimes forget to turn off the lights or the air conditioners (空调). As a result, a lot of electricity is wasted. Thanks to AI, the problem can be solved. It learns what the temperature is and how many people are inside the buildings. Then it makes thousands of small changes to save electricity every day. No single change is big, but all of them together can make a big difference.

Another problem is about hunting wild animals. You can’t imagine how many kinds of wild animals around the world are in danger now. Luckily, AI can collect all the data (数据) to learn from the past hunting events. Then it can guess where the hunters will go next. It was once used in a certain area, and the number of hunting events dropped from 19 a month to zero.

How can AI help reduce pollution? To clean up plastic waste from the ocean, you first need to know where it is. However, it’s difficult because the ocean is too wide. But with satellites (人造卫星), AI can quickly make a map to show where the plastic is. This helps clean up the ocean much more efficiently, because the ships can be sent to the right places to collect the plastic waste quickly.
However, none of these benefits come for free. Training AI also uses a lot of energy. So we should make wise choices.
source: 真题/2026年湖南省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Do you read fairy tales (童话)? Have you ever dreamed of stepping into a fairy tale? If so, in Germany, your dream will come true. Here, the German Fairy Tale Route can take you through ancient castles (城堡), thick forests and unusual villages—just like those in the stories we all know and love.

This special route (路线), a 600-kilometer road, was set up in 1975 to remember the Brothers Grimm, two famous German storytellers—Jacob Grimm and his younger brother Wilhelm. Together, they collected and wrote hundreds of stories, and then published (刊登) them in a book called Grimm’s Fairy Tales. Some of their well-known stories include Cinderella, Snow White, Hansel and Gretel, and Sleeping Beauty.

The route starts in Hanau, the town where the Brothers Grimm were born. From there, it winds north through beautiful countryside. Along the route, visitors can see the childhood home of the Grimm brothers in Steinau and the university town of Marburg, where they studied. In Alsfeld, you can walk through Little Red Riding Hood country and imagine meeting the much-loved girl in her red hat. The route also passes through Hamelin, the setting of The Pied Piper of Hamelin, and ends in Bremen, where a statue (雕塑) of the Bremen Town Musicians welcomes visitors.

Throughout the year, the German Fairy Tale Route hosts many events that breathe new life into old stories. Visitors can enjoy movies, folk festivals, storytelling evenings, to name but a few. It’s more than just a journey through picturesque places. It takes you right into the heart of storytelling itself.
So pack your imagination and get ready for an unforgettable journey!
source: 真题/2026年湖南省长沙市中考英语试题.docx

paras: Now picture this: You are spending two weeks in a foreign country helping local kids with Chinese in the morning and sunbathing on a beach in the afternoon. That’s exactly what voluntourism is all about. “Voluntourism” is a blend (混合) of “volunteering” and “tourism”. It means doing volunteer work in the place where one is vacationing.

Voluntourism has many advantages. For local communities, volunteers bring energy, skills and kindness. They build houses, clean the environment, provide medical care, and so on. As for voluntourists, they get free meals and housing when volunteering. Also, it’s a great way to learn about other cultures while making a positive (积极的) change.

But there are problems too. First, some people say short-term voluntourism does not create lasting change. Building a house in one week might not be as helpful as training local workers. Another problem is that sometimes volunteers take away jobs and income (收入) from the locals. Also, some projects are not well planned. As a result, they may fail to meet expectations, and even do harm to both voluntourists and local communities.

So, what should you do if you want to be a good voluntourist? First, research carefully. Choose a responsible organization (负责任的机构) that listens to local people. Then, think about what skills you have to help those in need. Besides, consider the value of what you do: Does it meet the community’s needs? Is it sustainable (可持续的)? When asking yourself these questions, always remember: Helping isn’t just about you feeling good—it’s about doing real good.

Voluntourism could be a wonderful experience if done right. However, if it is done wrong, things will be different. The key is to make informed decisions that will leave the world better than it was when you started.
source: 真题/2026年湖南省长沙市中考英语试题.docx

paras: Many people think birds have simple minds, but ravens (渡鸦) are a surprising exception. Their intelligence has long been compared to that of monkeys and even humans. One of the most surprising things they can do is to make plans for the future.

In one experiment, ravens were trained to use a tool to get food. Later, they were given a choice among several things, including the tool and some useless objects. Most of the ravens chose the tool, even with no immediate food reward. This showed they could remember how to use the tool and plan ahead to get the treat later.

Ravens are good at solving real-life problems. They use sticks to dig insects out of trees, and some even drop nuts (坚果) on roads so cars can crack them open. They can solve problems that require several steps, like using a short stick to get a longer one, then using the long stick to reach food.

Their intelligence isn’t just about solving problems. Ravens have rich social lives. They remember different faces, including those of other ravens and humans. They can hold grudges against people who have treated them badly, and even teach their young to stay away from those people.

Sadly, many kinds of ravens are suffering from habitat (栖息地) loss and pollution. As we learn more about their intelligence, scientists hope people will see them as more than just “common birds” and take action to protect them.
source: 真题/2026年广东省深圳市中考英语试题.docx

paras: This March, fifteen international students formed a Gen Z APEC Reporters team and visited the 2026 Greater Bay Area Flower Show in Shenzhen. The event was the first youth communication activity of the APEC “China Year” in Shenzhen.

The students walked through creatively designed gardens. They took photos and shared stories about green development from a global perspective. The event aimed to show Shenzhen as a “city of parks” and spread green ideas.

A French student loved the flowers. Two Russian students admired the iris (鸢尾花), which is this year’s theme flower. One of them praised the Dapeng garden for its bright colors. A student from Turkmenistan was deeply moved by the Nanshan garden, calling it shiny and bright. A Nigerian student said that being in nature brings peace and relaxation.

Besides enjoying the views, the students also documented (记录) their visit in many ways. One Russian student wrote a blog post highlighting the City Garden of Shenzhen, while another made short videos for online sharing. The visitors said they would continue to document Shenzhen’s green development through videos and posts, presenting an eco-friendly and open city to the world.

“Gardens are small, but they carry big ideas of green development,” one member said. “We are honored to tell Shenzhen’s stories and strengthen communication between the Greater Bay Area and the world.”

The flower show ran through April 6, bringing together designers and works from APEC member economies across four sections (部分)—Master Garden, Bay Area Garden, City Garden, and Floral Market—along with eight mini-gardens, showing over 30 fantastic creations. The team will continue to visit key places of Shenzhen’s APEC-themed activities, recording the city’s development and sharing its youthful energy with the world.
source: 真题/2026年广东省深圳市中考英语试题.docx

paras: Researchers from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) have estimated (估计) that the world may need about 1 billion new homes by 2050. According to a researcher from MIT, if people use wood to make so many homes, an area of forest more than three times the size of the Amazon rainforest may be cut down. The MIT researchers tried to find other materials to take the place of wood to make house parts. And they found recycled plastic could play a role.

The MIT team discovered that recycled plastic mixed with bits of glass could be used as a new material to make trusses (桁架)—supports put under floors to make sure that the floors can carry the weight of everything on them.

The MIT team wanted to know how much weight the trusses could carry. In a test, they 3D printed four trusses with the new material. Each truss weighed only about 6 kg—lighter than a comparable wooden truss. The team put the four trusses under a wooden floor model and slowly added heavy weights on the floor. Through the test, the team found the four trusses could sustain objects weighing more than 1,800 kg—about the weight of a car. This showed trusses made from the new material were strong enough to be used in house building in America.

The finding may benefit house building a lot. It will be much easier to send house parts made from this new material to different places. What’s more, the researchers say it is possible to bring down the cost of making house parts. The researchers hope that one day they can 3D print more house parts with the new material, so that more used plastic could be turned into something useful.
source: 真题/2026年广西中考英语试题.docx

paras: Climate change is often talked about, yet the change in the seasons—warmer winters and hotter summers—may not be noticed because it happens very slowly. Studies show people don’t notice slow changes easily. The story of Princeton is a good example.

In the past, Lake Carnegie froze every winter. People in Princeton could skate on the thick ice through winter. However, around the 1970s, winters in Princeton started to become warmer. Now, the lake seldom freezes, so people cannot skate on it every winter. But most people there didn’t connect this with climate change.

The real-life example helped researchers look for a better way to get people to notice slow changes brought by climate change. In their research, they showed volunteers two different graphs (图表)—a temperature graph and a lake-freezing graph. The temperature graph showed a fictional (虚构的) town’s rising winter temperatures over the years. The lake-freezing graph showed whether the town’s lake froze each year. Both graphs showed the same climate trend (趋势), but they made the volunteers feel differently. When the volunteers saw the lake-freezing graph, they felt climate change was more serious, because they could directly see the lake didn’t freeze every year like before. This helped them see the influence of climate change clearly. But when the volunteers saw the temperature graph, they didn’t feel the same, because the graph failed to help them connect climate change with daily life.
With the help of what the research has found, we can actively notice slow changes in our daily life brought by climate change. At the same time, we can also help the people around us notice them.
source: 真题/2026年广西中考英语试题.docx

paras: By 2030, the world’s data (数据) centers are expected to use more than double the electricity they use today. AI is the main driver. It forces countries to look for new ways to solve the big problem. China is leading the way by putting data centers under the sea as a greener solution.
In December 2022, Hainan became home to China’s first underwater data center. This was followed by a more advanced (先进的) project in Shanghai in 2025.

AI servers give off heat while working, making the temperature rise. If the heat isn’t taken away in time, the servers won’t run well and may even break down. On-land data centers have to use up to 40% of their electricity just for cooling AI servers.

Underwater data centers, like the one in Shanghai, use pipes to pump (输送) seawater. Seawater goes through the radiators on the back of the servers. It takes in heat and carries it away. The sea temperature is about 15°C, perfect for natural cooling. In this way, electricity is saved. An assessment (评估) from the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology shows the underwater data center uses at least 30% less electricity than on-land data centers thanks to natural cooling.

Underwater data centers can also reduce land usage by 80%. And the one in Shanghai offers another benefit: it will get more than 95% of its electricity from a kind of renewable energy—wind energy. And the use of tidal (潮汐) and wave energy is also taken into consideration.

China’s efforts in developing underwater data centers show its promise to create low-carbon digital infrastructure (低碳数字基础设施). The move not only helps reduce the environmental impact of AI, but also could set a new standard for sustainable computing (可持续算力) worldwide.
source: 真题/2026年重庆市中考英语试题.docx

paras: Scientists tell how healthy rainforests are by listening to the sounds of their wildlife. A healthy forest is alive with animal calls and birdsong but an unhealthy forest is much quieter. However, that is a big job. Researchers can make thousands of hours of recordings but then someone has to listen to them all and pick out the different animal and bird calls.

What if that someone is an AI though? Scientists are using AI technology to help with the task. Through the new Forest Listeners web experiment, scientists want people around the world—including you—to help too.

The site gets you to move around a virtual (虚拟的) forest, listening for wildlife. When you find a new species (物种), you listen to its song until you can remember it. The next step is to listen to real forest recordings (there are more than 1.2 million of them), and decide for each one whether you can hear that animal call, can’t hear it or aren’t sure.

The answers people give are then used to train AI to identify animals by their sounds. Scientists say that the project helps them process a huge number of recordings. Without AI, it would take many years to study them all. “Every sound tagged (贴标签) by a forest listener helps train our AI models,” the scientists said. “This group effort provides us with valuable information, allowing us to notice small changes in species’ presence and behavior. These are important signs of a healthy forest.”
source: 真题/2026年四川省成都市中考英语试题.docx

paras: Everyone sleeps. Good sleep helps you get enough rest and stay energetic. While you sleep, your brain processes the information it has received during the day and forms memories. Also, your body does lots of repair work—refreshing tired body parts, reducing pains and cleaning up waste in your body.

Today, people sleep through the night. However, diaries, books and other records from the 15th to 17th centuries suggest people used to sleep differently. People would go to sleep between 9 pm and 11 pm for a couple of hours. They would wake up for a while, and during this period they might read a book, visit a neighbor or do some chores. Afterwards, they would lie down for the second sleep, which lasted until morning. Researchers think it was the invention of the light bulb in 1879 that changed this. Electric lights meant people started staying up later, so when they finally went to bed, they slept until morning.

The Industrial Revolution (工业革命) also changed how people slept. Starting in the 18th century, people moved from the countryside to the city to work in the factories. People had to get up and start work at a certain time. To make sure people didn’t oversleep, knocker-uppers, also known as wake-up helpers, appeared. They made money by waking people up. Every morning, they would walk down the street knocking on doors or windows with sticks. As alarm clocks grew popular in the 1930s and 1940s, knocker-uppers weren’t needed any more.

Today, our sleep is mainly influenced by both social pressure and electronic products. Falling asleep becomes hard and sleep quality goes down. Put screens away 30 to 60 minutes before bedtime. Keep a comfortable bedroom temperature, avoid bright light and reduce nearby noise. These will help you relax and wind down. If you have lots of thoughts or worries, writing them down before bedtime can help you put them aside for the night.
source: 真题/2026年四川省成都市中考英语试题.docx

paras: Do you know the Ali Plateau? It is a very cold area which is nearly 5,000 meters above sea level in the western part of China. Qi Fabao, the “hero regiment commander for defending the border” (卫国戍边英雄团长), has guarded our land with his life there.

Qi Fabao was born into an ordinary family in Wuwei City, Gansu Province. He was always a top student at school in his childhood and had a strong wish to join the army. At the age of 18, he realized his dream. He chose to set foot on the land of the Ali Plateau in Xizang and began his career of defending the border. He said, “Not everyone can understand my choice, but I have never regretted it.”

For over 20 years, he has defended the border and experienced many life-and-death moments. When the communication lines didn’t work, he stood in the cold water for hours to repair them. When facing the falling stones, he even used his body to stop them. Once in 2005, he rode a horse in the snow mountains to carry out a task. His horse fell off the cliff (悬崖), and he was thrown onto the edge of the cliff. His back was badly hurt, but the great pain never broke him. More than 1,000 patrols (巡逻) saw his promise to defend the border of our land.
With his youth and blood, Qi Fabao has written a chapter of loyalty (忠诚) and responsibility. He shows us that loving our country is not empty words, but real actions.
source: 真题/2026年云南省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Desertification (荒漠化) is a difficult problem for the whole world. For many years, Chinese scientists have had rich experience in dealing with desertification in Northwest China. Now they are working to help African countries turn their sandy areas into green ones.

China has made great progress through hard work, though it is seriously affected by desertification. By November 2024, China had built a long wall of trees, which caught the world’s attention. It is 3,046 km long! And China has created 32 million hectares (公顷) of new forest.

Chinese scientists shared the technologies with Mauritania, an African country. They introduced different kinds of plants from China and used straw checkerboards to stop sand from moving. They developed new ways to save water for farming. Smart technologies such as robots, drones and sand-blocking systems (阻沙系统) driven by solar panels also helped a lot.

The China-Africa Green Technology Park was built in Mauritania. In 2024, the park was empty land swept by wind and sand. Just one year later, there were grasses, fruits and vegetables. Wang Yongdong, a senior engineer from China, said, “The goal of the park is not only to protect the environment but also to help local people.” So far, China has trained 45 skilled workers and created 120 jobs for the local community.

The Mauritanian environment minister (部长) described China as a “very important partner”. To help African countries, Chinese scientists have overcome many difficulties. As a key member fighting against desertification in the world, China promises to keep working and make bigger efforts. Wang said, “We are a community with a shared future. We hope our efforts will show this spirit.”
source: 真题/2026年云南省中考英语试题.docx

paras: This is a true story of a four-legged hero as well as animal friendship and care. Everything took place in Nairobi, Kenya—a country in East Africa.

When she was just a few weeks old, a small elephant sadly lost her mother to a poacher attack (盗猎袭击). Luckily, the little elephant was found by a farmer and taken to an elephant orphanage where she was named Natumi. There, at the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, Natumi was safe, but very scared and shy. Soon, however, new orphaned baby elephants began to arrive at the shelter. At first, Natumi hid behind her keeper’s legs, but it soon became clear that the other baby elephants needed someone to depend on. They were very young and many of them had injuries (外伤；损伤) like wounds and scratches. To everyone’s surprise, shy little Natumi stepped up to the task. She began to act like a big sister to the seven other elephants, keeping them calm and playing with them in the surrounding bush (周边的荒野). Guided by Natumi, the elephants had soon formed their own loving family. In the end, the new family of elephants was strong and healthy enough to return to the wild—but the workers at the shelter would never forget a little elephant named Natumi who made it possible.
source: 真题/2026年陕西省中考英语试题.docx

paras: Water pollution is a serious problem around the world, and it is difficult to deal with. Traditional water sensors (传感器) can only work in fixed places. As a result, they cannot cover large water bodies like rivers, lakes or oceans. To solve this problem, scientists created a bionic (仿生) tool—a robotic fish.

The robotic fish is a great example of bionics. It shows how scientists copy nature to solve problems. In fact, the idea of copying nature is not new. The Wright brothers created their first plane by studying the flight of birds. Modern scientists created robotic fish by studying the swimming skills of trout (鳟鱼). Trout are good at moving fast in water with very little energy. By “learning” the way trout move, robotic fish can work for ten hours after they are fully charged.

According to scientists, the robotic fish has a special soft tail, so it can swim quietly and smoothly under water. It will not scare water animals or harm the underwater environment. Because of the small sensors inside its “body”, it can “taste” water to find harmful things. Once the robotic fish finds water pollution, it will send a warning message to a central computer at once. The robotic fish can even “eat” small pieces of plastic in water bodies and repair itself when it gets broken. Now more and more robotic fish are being used in rivers, lakes and oceans all over the world. They work together as a team to reduce water pollution.

By copying nature, scientists have offered lots of possibilities for protecting the environment and improving people’s lives. As one scientist said, “Nature is our best teacher. This invention shows people’s creativity and the value of learning from nature.”
source: 真题/2026年宁夏回族自治区中考英语试题.docx

paras: Do you sometimes get angry? Perhaps your answer is yes. Actually, everyone feels angry sometimes. It’s part of being human. However, anger is a strong feeling and it is not easy to control. Sometimes anger can be good, because it can encourage us to change things that make us unhappy.

“Anger is a normal feeling and it’s OK to have these feelings sometimes,” says Dr Nathwani, a psychologist (心理学家). It’s common for teenagers to feel angry. First, the body’s hormones (荷尔蒙) are changing, which can make feelings much stronger. Second, the part of the brain that helps to manage feelings doesn’t fully develop until you’re in your mid-20s.

Being angry does not mean you are a grumpy (脾气坏的) person. Sometimes it suggests something else. “Anger usually comes when we feel hurt, scared or unhappy,” says Dr Nathwani. “It can be a strong feeling that we notice in our bodies. We may feel hot or our hearts may beat fast.” Sometimes you might not even know why you’re feeling this way. Your anger is not always caused by your own stress or other people being unkind. Not being understood by friends or family can also make you angry.

Although it’s OK to feel angry sometimes, it’s not healthy when anger takes over. You might act in a negative way and it can make you hurt others or yourself. Next time you feel angry, try these simple ways to calm down. You can take a deep breath. Deep breathing helps your body get away from the “angry energy”. Taking some time to relax is also a good choice. For example, you can take a short walk, listen to soft music or do simple exercise. Share your feelings with someone you trust. It gives you a break from feeling unhappy all alone. When you talk to them about your anger, they might help you see things in a calmer way.
source: 真题/2026年宁夏回族自治区中考英语试题.docx

paras: People are talking a lot about artificial intelligence (AI), viewing it as a force that could reshape how society works. But there is something important missing from this discussion. It isn’t enough to ask how it will change us. We also need to understand how we shape AI and what it can tell us about ourselves.

Every AI model we develop mirrors our rules and expresses our beliefs. A few years ago, while looking for new workers, a famous company gave up an AI-powered tool after finding it unfavorable to women. The AI was not designed to behave this way; instead, it was influenced by the historical data (数据) favoring men. Similarly, a recent study found that lending algorithms (算法) often offer less favorable terms to people of color, worsening long-standing unfairness in the money-lending business. In both cases, AI isn’t creating new biases (偏见); it is mirroring the ones that are already present.

These reflections (反映) give us an important chance to take a close look at ourselves. By making these problems visible and more pressing, AI challenges us to recognize and address what causes algorithmic bias. As AI continues to develop, we must ask ourselves how we as average people want to shape its role in society. We should not only improve AI models, but also make sure that AI is developed and used responsibly.

A number of companies are already taking action. They are judging the data, rules, and beliefs that shape the behavior of AI models. Still, we cannot expect the companies to do all the work. As long as AI is trained on human data, it will reflect human behavior. That means we have to think carefully about the footprints of ourselves we leave in the world. I may value privacy, but if I give it up in a heartbeat to visit a website, the algorithms may make a very different judgment of what I really want and what is good for me. If I want meaningful human connections yet spend more time on social media and less time in the physical company of my friends, I am indirectly training AI models about the true nature of humanity.

As AI becomes more powerful, we need to take increasing care to read our principles (原则) into the record of our actions rather than allowing the two to diverge. Recognizing this allows us to make better decisions, but only when we are prepared to look closely and take responsibility for what we see.
source: 真题/2025年北京市中考英语真题.docx

paras: Every morning, a big riverside school in the forest of Borneo comes to life. The caretakers and teachers in the school are from a specialized team, and the students there are orangutans (猩猩) whose parents have gone missing, making it one of the most unusual schools in the world.

The orangutans aged from 2 to 8 are divided into five groups according to their skills. They are looked after by the team who feed the babies and teach the older ones to start feeding themselves. There are often problems in the beginning. For example, there was a lesson about how to break open a coconut to drink the milk inside. Several young orangutans couldn’t do that and they got very angry about the whole thing.

Of course, as in any social group, the orangutans have to learn to get on with each other. There are the usual arguments over food when one orangutan doesn’t get what he or she wants. However, with the care of the trainers, they gradually learn to accept each other.

In one of the lessons, the trainers taught young orangutans to climb trees. This is an important skill they need to learn. Some of the orangutans in particular were really scared. It took them a long time to get the courage to climb up and swing from a branch (树枝), but when they finally did it, they were so satisfied with themselves!

The goal of the “education system” is to train the orangutans to be able to live in the wild again and look after themselves. They won’t have to stay at school forever. After the older orangutans are set free into the forest, there is no more connection with the people from the school. They now have to live as wild orangutans again and be accepted by the other orangutans who are already there.

The day when they say goodbye is a difficult one. However, the trainers are happy that their job is done. They have successfully taught young orangutans how to live in the wild again—where they belong.
source: 真题/2025年山东省济南市中考英语真题.docx

paras: Construction (建筑) is one of the biggest users of energy and one of the biggest polluters. According to AI Magazine, construction is responsible for using 38% of world energy. The building part alone accounts for almost 55% of electricity use and 33% of greenhouse gases. It’s also well known that steel produces too much material waste in building construction.

Because of this big challenge, the future of sustainable (可持续的) construction may lie with AI. AI is able to study building efficiency (效率) performance by grouping data to find the best chances for sustainable material usage. With a tool like AI, the future of sustainable construction could progress much faster than in the past. Besides, AI helps architects (建筑师) work with new tools and sustainable materials to create better buildings and cities of the future. For example, construction 3D printing guided by AI can offer better choices for building materials to save money, and map out how construction materials could be recycled.

In a professional article, AI is praised as a tool for sustainable construction: “In recent years, AI has become a promising tool for construction. AI can examine a large number of data sets on weather conditions and help to make full use of building systems for energy efficiency, water protection and other goals.”

AI can be used to speed up the future of sustainable construction, set standards for the industry, and make construction more efficient and affordable. Like any other computer program, AI is a tool that is particularly good at studying data sets, but for the moment it still requires smart and ethical (有道德的) human beings to lead its work. All of that has to be done with respect for humans, so it’s really up to us to make it work.
source: 真题/2025年山东省济南市中考英语真题.docx

paras: “What do you think I should do?” asks your friend, as she sits beside you, waiting for your advice. This is no easy situation. Say something your friend disagrees with or something unhelpful, and you might feel you’ve disappointed her.

It’s human nature to want to offer solutions when someone comes to you with a problem. It’s also easy to fall into the trap of simply saying “Everything will be OK”. This is not actually useful for your friend. But we often say that because we believe we need to say something. This is because we’re glad that our friend has come to us for help, even if we don’t really think we’re able to give it. So is it a good idea to try to give advice at all? The answer is yes… if it’s done in the right way.

In fact, friends often really only want someone to listen to them. It’s important to try to work out whether they’re actually asking for advice, or simply wanting to talk over whatever is going round in their head. Talking may make people feel better all by itself. There’s no harm in asking whether they’d like you to give suggestions.

It’s also important to be honest. If you’re unable to think of a way to solve your friends’ problem, just say so. Your friends won’t feel upset, and you can still listen carefully and try to put yourself in their shoes. Then you can go away and try to think of something helpful. You can ask yourself, “What would I do if I were to experience the same thing?” Later you can go back to your friends with a few helpful suggestions.

Sometimes a problem doesn’t go away overnight. It can be hard to listen to your friends going over and over the same thing without being able to help them. They will certainly be thankful if you just allow them to “talk it out”, though. Maybe they’re building up courage to take action, and need to convince (说服) themselves they’re doing the right thing. Just being there for them may be all you have to do to make things better.

paras: In many cases, you may find yourself or somebody faking (假笑) a smile in photos. Why can one easily discover a fake smile and why does it seem so difficult to give a real smile in photos?

Scientists have found that a real smile is characterized by two main muscle (肌肉) movements. When we smile, we lift our mouth upwards and cause the skin around our eyes to gather into folds. These muscle movements are usually absent in the case of a forced smile, especially when the smile is small. Our brains are highly skilled at distinguishing the differences in muscle movements. That’s why though trying to fake a real smile can be hard, discovering a fake one on someone else is a piece of cake.

One of the most common reasons why you look unnatural in photos is an increased awareness (意识) of your appearance. The worry about posture, hair, and makeup can add to the stress, killing the chances of a real smile. A smile looks best when it comes naturally. Warm and welcoming smiles come along with warm and welcoming body language, but when you’re in front of the camera, trying too hard to perform can make your body language appear stiff (僵硬的) and far from welcoming.

Besides, facial expressions are not always understood in the same way. A smile can mean different things in different cultures. For example, a wide smile that seems welcoming to some may appear fake and dishonest to others. This may also influence how people feel about your smile in photos.

However, we shouldn’t let this trouble us too much. So, if you want to smile naturally before the camera, perhaps the simplest trick is to give your brain a real reason to feel happy. Maybe recall a joyful moment or just think back to a funny story you read… that should work!

paras: In the early 1900s, Austrian scientist Karl von Frisch discovered the “waggle dance” of honey bees. They dance to communicate where to find food, showing an advanced form of communication. His discovery suggested that bees seem to “think” much like humans. Bees can count up to four and even use knowledge learned in one situation in new ones. Another amazing ability they have is similar to that of a few mammals (like dolphins, rats, and some monkeys)—metacognition (元认知).

Studying bees’ brains is challenging, but scientists have found ways. One such scientist is Clint Perry from Queen Mary University of London. He designed experiments (实验) where bees chose between two spots, one above and one below a black bar. If they landed above, they got a sweet drink; if below, a terrible one. Perry made the test easier or harder by moving the landing spots further from or closer to the black bar. Perry found that bees avoided difficult tests and tried easy ones, suggesting they can judge (判断) their chances of “passing”.

This ability to make decisions in advance according to their chances of success is similar to how humans choose whether to take a test. However, Perry admits we can’t be sure if bees are truly judging by their own knowledge or just avoiding an unpleasant taste.

Although there is much uncertainty, the discovery of metacognition in bees opens up new possibilities. It suggests that bees’ tiny brains may be quite capable (有能力的). It could be that skills such as simple math and navigation take far less actual brainpower than we thought. While bees aren’t as smart as mammals in memory and language, studying their brains could help us understand how our own brains process information.

We may also have to rethink how we view the rest of the insect world. There are an awful lot of small insects flying around in the garden and crawling underground. Who knows what those tiny minds might be capable of?
